title.narrative: Campaign for the Protection of the Oceans and Implementation of Sustainable Development Goal 14. Parliamentarians in target ODA-eligible countries take action on the new High Seas Treaty.
Ratification of the High Seas Treaty in ODA-eligible countries.

target.value: 50 member-parliamentarians attend PGA’s Third Parliamentary Oceans Day with a focus on the new High Seas Treaty and commit to advance ratification in their countries.

actual.value: 62 member-parliamentarians attended PGA’s Third Parliamentary Oceans Day, including 49 MPs from ODA-eligible countries. In 2023, PGA provided its members with technical assistance upon request, including with background materials, such as the publication of the Factsheet for Parliamentarians on the High Seas. The 3rd Consultative Assembly for Parliamentarians on the Oceans (CAP-Oceans) was held during the 44th PGA Annual Parliamentary Forum in November 2023 and resulted in the adoption of the Victoria Plan of Action. The plan described commitments and follow up actions parliamentarians can take to further the objectives of this Campaign. As a result, Vanuatu signed the Treaty on November 30, 2023. Seychelles – host of the 3rd CAP-Oceans – became the third country to ratify the treaty in March 2024.

target.value: 10 more parliaments ratify the High Seas Treaty.

title.narrative: SDG Target 16.3 –PGA’s Campaign to Abolish the Death Penalty contributes to abolish the use of capital punishment, widen parliamentary support for international instruments on abolition and ensures that abolitionist countries, which apply a moratorium, do not reintroduce capital punishment in their criminal laws or resume executions.

PGA member-parliamentarians take concrete actions in support of national legislative initiatives in an ODA-eligible country for the abolition of the death penalty or moratorium on capital punishment, such as in Guyana and Morocco.

target.value: At least one ODA-eligible country abolishes the death penalty or moratorium on capital punishment.
At least one national legislative initiative in an ODA-eligible country for the abolition of the death penalty or for restrictions on its use.

actual.value: PGA made major progress in limiting the scope of the use of capital punishment in 2023, contributing to progress and providing technical assistance upon request. As a result: 1. The Parliament of Ghana adopted a Bill abolishing the death penalty for ordinary crimes, which was assented by the President on August 11, 2023. 2. The Parliament of Malaysia passed 2 bills abolishing the mandatory death penalty for 12 offences. The bills entered into force on July 4 and September 11, 2023. This was the culmination of PGA’s efforts on this issue in Malaysia since 2012. 3. In Pakistan, the parliament passed the “Control of Narcotics Substances Act. 2023,” which removed capital punishment for drug trafficking convictions. The law was enacted on August 5. PGA’s Death Penalty Campaign has been active in the country since 2016. 4. Armenia ratified Protocol 13 to the ECHR, concerning the abolition of the death penalty in all circumstances, in October 2023.
